card.name: End of subject noun before "is unknown"
card.fires_on: The last word of a long noun phrase that is the subject of a sentence about unknown or unstudied effects, such as "the effect of X on Y". It fires on the noun just before the verb, for example "is unknown" or "has not been evaluated".

modes.label: Drug or enzyme group noun
modes.description: Final piece of a plural drug, metabolite or substrate term ending the subject phrase.
modes.example: The effect of induction or inhibition of other pathways on exposure to alosetron and its metabol<<ites>> is not known.

modes.label: Population or route noun
modes.description: Final noun of a phrase naming a patient group or route of use, before a statement of unknown risk or no evaluation.
modes.example: The background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage for the indicated<< population>> is unknown.

card.writes: The suppressed overview and description words suggest it pushes toward a verb phrase continuing the sentence rather than a heading.
card.plain: It marks the end of the subject in sentences saying an effect or risk is unknown or not studied.
